=== #1988
## Context

While regenerating `frontend/a11y-baseline.json` for #1981 (the useId→ancestry keying fix, review finding 1), the `run detail` case in `frontend/e2e/a11y.spec.ts` produced a DIFFERENT gated-violation count depending on how it was invoked:

- Run standalone, or preceded only by the `results` test (`playwright test e2e/a11y.spec.ts -g "results|run detail"`): **13** serious/critical violations, stable across 3 repeats.
- Run as part of the full 8-test spec file (`dashboard` → `connections` → `suites list` → `suite detail` → `results` → `run detail` → `assets` → `admin`, the sequence CI and `pnpm a11y:baseline` both use): **0** violations, stable across repeated full-suite runs.

Each test gets its own fresh Playwright page/context (no shared storage), so this isn't a stale-session issue. The likely cause: the Results table's "first row" (`page.locator('tr.ant-table-row').first()`) resolves to a *different seeded run* depending on how much wall-clock time/backend state has passed before the `run detail` test executes, and only some runs' detail pages render a muted `ant-typography-secondary` caption that fails `color-contrast`. That capping element differs per run's data.

## Impact

The committed baseline for `route:/results/:id` (currently **0** rows, reflecting the deterministic-in-CI full-suite sequence) is only correct for that exact invocation order. A future `pnpm a11y:baseline` regen run that inserts, removes, or reorders a test in `e2e/a11y.spec.ts` — or one run manually with a subset of tests (`-g`) — will likely see a nonzero count for this surface again and could file it as a "new violation" when it's actually the same underlying issue reappearing.

## Suggested fix

Pick the run-detail target deterministically instead of "first row in whatever order the table currently renders" — e.g. click a row identified by suite/check name, or add an explicit `ORDER BY` tie-break to the `runs` list endpoint so `least-recently-inserted`/`id` decides ties instead of relying on `started_at` (which the demo seed can produce with duplicate values). Re-verify with the same standalone-vs-full-suite comparison this issue used to find the bug.

Filed per CONTRIBUTING rule 3a — found live, verified real (not test noise), deferred because it's outside the scope of #1981's three review findings.

=== #1671
Item 2 of the Theme-3 accessibility plan — highest user-impact single item. Severity is communicated almost entirely by color today (red/orange/green tags, recharts series where color is the ONLY encoding). Add icons/shapes/text beside color everywhere severity or status renders, and adopt a colorblind-safe palette. ~8% of male users can't reliably read the current severity language. Includes the dashboards' chart series. Reduced-motion support rides along per the plan's item 5 (cheap here).

=== #1672
Item 3 of the Theme-3 accessibility plan: full keyboard traversal of the screen set; focus-trap + restore on the surviving drawers/modals (Share, version history, run progress, import); visible focus states; skip-to-content. antd gives a decent baseline — the custom drawer/table/editor compositions are where it breaks. Verify in a real browser (the jsdom-proves-nothing lesson, #1282).

=== #1673
Item 4 of the Theme-3 accessibility plan: landmarks; headers/captions on the results/runs tables; aria-live for async run-progress updates; and a text alternative for every chart — the dashboards are pure-visual today. A data-table fallback per chart covers both a11y and the PDF-export path (#345 shipped as #1122). New code stops hard-coding user-facing strings now (i18n stays deferred, but don't make it worse — plan item 5).

1. **`color-contrast` on `.ant-typography-secondary`** (86 of 107) — a theme-token change, likely one PR, likely folds into [#1671](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1671)'s colorblind-safe palette work rather than a separate pass.
2. **`label` on filter `Select`s** (17) — associate the visible label text via `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` on the antd `Select`'s underlying input; concentrated on Results and Suites.

The baseline was captured against the CI-equivalent stack (Postgres+Redis+OpenBao, migrated + seeded, uvicorn dev-bypass API, Vite) plus the OTP stack for the sign-in route, and is stable across repeated captures (the raw axe selector for a couple of `Select` instances turned out to be flaky — a React `useId()`-minted id that isn't stable across page loads — so the ratchet's selector-matching normalizes those out before comparing; see `frontend/scripts/a11y/ratchet.ts`).

=== #1988
## Context

While regenerating `frontend/a11y-baseline.json` for #1981 (the useId→ancestry keying fix, review finding 1), the `run detail` case in `frontend/e2e/a11y.spec.ts` produced a DIFFERENT gated-violation count depending on how it was invoked:

- Run standalone, or preceded only by the `results` test (`playwright test e2e/a11y.spec.ts -g "results|run detail"`): **13** serious/critical violations, stable across 3 repeats.
- Run as part of the full 8-test spec file (`dashboard` → `connections` → `suites list` → `suite detail` → `results` → `run detail` → `assets` → `admin`, the sequence CI and `pnpm a11y:baseline` both use): **0** violations, stable across repeated full-suite runs.

Each test gets its own fresh Playwright page/context (no shared storage), so this isn't a stale-session issue. The likely cause: the Results table's "first row" (`page.locator('tr.ant-table-row').first()`) resolves to a *different seeded run* depending on how much wall-clock time/backend state has passed before the `run detail` test executes, and only some runs' detail pages render a muted `ant-typography-secondary` caption that fails `color-contrast`. That capping element differs per run's data.

## Impact

The committed baseline for `route:/results/:id` (currently **0** rows, reflecting the deterministic-in-CI full-suite sequence) is only correct for that exact invocation order. A future `pnpm a11y:baseline` regen run that inserts, removes, or reorders a test in `e2e/a11y.spec.ts` — or one run manually with a subset of tests (`-g`) — will likely see a nonzero count for this surface again and could file it as a "new violation" when it's actually the same underlying issue reappearing.

## Suggested fix

Pick the run-detail target deterministically instead of "first row in whatever order the table currently renders" — e.g. click a row identified by suite/check name, or add an explicit `ORDER BY` tie-break to the `runs` list endpoint so `least-recently-inserted`/`id` decides ties instead of relying on `started_at` (which the demo seed can produce with duplicate values). Re-verify with the same standalone-vs-full-suite comparison this issue used to find the bug.

Filed per CONTRIBUTING rule 3a — found live, verified real (not test noise), deferred because it's outside the scope of #1981's three review findings.

=== #1671
Item 2 of the Theme-3 accessibility plan — highest user-impact single item. Severity is communicated almost entirely by color today (red/orange/green tags, recharts series where color is the ONLY encoding). Add icons/shapes/text beside color everywhere severity or status renders, and adopt a colorblind-safe palette. ~8% of male users can't reliably read the current severity language. Includes the dashboards' chart series. Reduced-motion support rides along per the plan's item 5 (cheap here).

=== #1672
Item 3 of the Theme-3 accessibility plan: full keyboard traversal of the screen set; focus-trap + restore on the surviving drawers/modals (Share, version history, run progress, import); visible focus states; skip-to-content. antd gives a decent baseline — the custom drawer/table/editor compositions are where it breaks. Verify in a real browser (the jsdom-proves-nothing lesson, #1282).

=== #1673
Item 4 of the Theme-3 accessibility plan: landmarks; headers/captions on the results/runs tables; aria-live for async run-progress updates; and a text alternative for every chart — the dashboards are pure-visual today. A data-table fallback per chart covers both a11y and the PDF-export path (#345 shipped as #1122). New code stops hard-coding user-facing strings now (i18n stays deferred, but don't make it worse — plan item 5).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Scratch stack for the docs screenshot/video lane (frontend/e2e-docs/).
# Mirrors CI's frontend-e2e job — dev-bypass auth, seeded demo data — on its
# own database, OpenBao KV mount and ports, so the developer's compose stack
# (and its orphan-secret sweep) never sees it. Reuses the compose Postgres
# (:5432), Redis (:6379, db 3) and OpenBao (:8200).
#
#   scripts/docs/capture-stack.sh start    # migrate + seed + api :8001 + vite :3001
#   scripts/docs/capture-stack.sh capture  # run the e2e-docs Playwright project
#   scripts/docs/capture-stack.sh stop     # stop the processes (data kept)
#   scripts/docs/capture-stack.sh destroy  # stop + drop the database + the KV mount
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
RUN="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dataq-docs-capture"
mkdir -p "$RUN"
API_PORT="${DOCS_API_PORT:-8001}"
WEB_PORT="${DOCS_WEB_PORT:-3001}"
DB_NAME="${DOCS_DB_NAME:-dataq_docs}"
KV_MOUNT="${DOCS_KV_MOUNT:-docs-capture}"
COMPOSE=(docker compose -f "$ROOT/docker-compose.yml")

_env() {
  set -a
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  source "$ROOT/.env"
  set +a
  export DATABASE_URL="REDACTED"
  export REDIS_URL="redis://localhost:6379/3"
  export SECRET_STORE=openbao
  export OPENBAO_ADDR="http://localhost:8200"
  export OPENBAO_TOKEN
  export OPENBAO_MOUNT="$KV_MOUNT"
  export AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true
  # Explicitly NOT OTP: a developer's .env.app may configure it, and OTP wins
  # over dev-bypass at import time (core/auth.py).
  export AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_EMAILS= AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_DOMAINS= AUTH_EMAIL_SMTP_HOST= AUTH_EMAIL_FROM=
  export DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL=
  export ENVIRONMENT=dev
  export REDACTED@dataq.local
  export RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false
  export DATAQ_ROLE_TOKENS_PATH="$RUN/.role-tokens.json"
}

_alive() { [ -f "$RUN/$1.pid" ] && kill -0 "$(cat "$RUN/$1.pid")" 2>/dev/null; }

_psql() { "${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T postgres psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d postgres -tAc "$1"; }

_bao() { curl -sf -X "$1" -H "X-Vault-Token: $OPENBAO_TOKEN" "http://localhost:8200/v1/$2" "${@:3}"; }

start() {
  _env
  if _alive api || _alive web; then
    echo "already running (pids in $RUN) — run 'stop' first"; exit 1
  fi
  _psql "select 1 from pg_database where datname='${DB_NAME}'" | grep -q 1 \
    || _psql "create database ${DB_NAME}" >/dev/null
  _bao GET "sys/mounts/${KV_MOUNT}" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || _bao POST "sys/mounts/${KV_MOUNT}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
         -d '{"type":"kv","options":{"version":"2"}}' >/dev/null
  (cd "$ROOT/backend" && conda run -n dataq --no-capture-output alembic upgrade head >"$RUN/alembic.log" 2>&1)
  (cd "$ROOT" && conda run -n dataq --no-capture-output python -m backend.scripts.seed_dev >"$RUN/seed.log" 2>&1)
  (cd "$ROOT" && nohup conda run -n dataq --no-capture-output \
      uvicorn backend.app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$API_PORT" >"$RUN/api.log" 2>&1 </dev/null & echo $! >"$RUN/api.pid")
  for _ in $(seq 1 40); do
    curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}/api/v1/me" >/dev/null && break; sleep 1
  done
  curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}/api/v1/me" >/dev/null || { echo "api did not come up"; tail -20 "$RUN/api.log"; exit 1; }
  # The seed carries no llm_settings row; the LLM captures need a saved, enabled
  # OpenAI-compatible config so a fresh stack regenerates the same images. The
  # key is a placeholder (Ollama ignores it); Test only shows OK when a server
  # answers at DOCS_LLM_BASE_URL.
  curl -sf -o /dev/null -X PUT -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    "http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}/api/v1/admin/llm" \
    -d "{\"provider\":\"openai_compatible\",\"model\":\"${DOCS_LLM_MODEL:-qwen2.5:14b}\",\"base_url\":\"${DOCS_LLM_BASE_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1}\",\"api_key\":\"docs-capture-placeholder\",\"structured_output\":\"prompt_json\",\"enabled\":true}" \
    || { echo "could not seed the LLM provider config"; exit 1; }
  # Optional: a real Snowflake reader connection + suite, for the SQL-generation and
  # suggest-checks captures (both need to introspect a live table — a fake config
  # errors on every call). Skipped when DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT is unset, so the base
  # capture set still works with no warehouse credentials at hand; export it (plus
  # DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_USER/_SECRET, the rest default to the harness reader's shape —

#   scripts/docs/capture-stack.sh capture  # run the e2e-docs Playwright project
#   scripts/docs/capture-stack.sh stop     # stop the processes (data kept)
#   scripts/docs/capture-stack.sh destroy  # stop + drop the database + the KV mount
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
RUN="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dataq-docs-capture"
mkdir -p "$RUN"
API_PORT="${DOCS_API_PORT:-8001}"
WEB_PORT="${DOCS_WEB_PORT:-3001}"
DB_NAME="${DOCS_DB_NAME:-dataq_docs}"
KV_MOUNT="${DOCS_KV_MOUNT:-docs-capture}"
COMPOSE=(docker compose -f "$ROOT/docker-compose.yml")

_env() {
  set -a
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  source "$ROOT/.env"
  set +a
  export DATABASE_URL="REDACTED"
  export REDIS_URL="redis://localhost:6379/3"
  export SECRET_STORE=openbao
  export OPENBAO_ADDR="http://localhost:8200"
  export OPENBAO_TOKEN
  export OPENBAO_MOUNT="$KV_MOUNT"
  export AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true
  # Explicitly NOT OTP: a developer's .env.app may configure it, and OTP wins
  # over dev-bypass at import time (core/auth.py).
  export AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_EMAILS= AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_DOMAINS= AUTH_EMAIL_SMTP_HOST= AUTH_EMAIL_FROM=
  export DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL=
  export ENVIRONMENT=dev
  export REDACTED@dataq.local
  export RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false
  export DATAQ_ROLE_TOKENS_PATH="$RUN/.role-tokens.json"
}

_alive() { [ -f "$RUN/$1.pid" ] && kill -0 "$(cat "$RUN/$1.pid")" 2>/dev/null; }

_psql() { "${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T postgres psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d postgres -tAc "$1"; }

_bao() { curl -sf -X "$1" -H "X-Vault-Token: $OPENBAO_TOKEN" "http://localhost:8200/v1/$2" "${@:3}"; }

start() {
  _env
  if _alive api || _alive web; then
    echo "already running (pids in $RUN) — run 'stop' first"; exit 1
  fi
  _psql "select 1 from pg_database where datname='${DB_NAME}'" | grep -q 1 \
    || _psql "create database ${DB_NAME}" >/dev/null
  _bao GET "sys/mounts/${KV_MOUNT}" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || _bao POST "sys/mounts/${KV_MOUNT}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
         -d '{"type":"kv","options":{"version":"2"}}' >/dev/null
  (cd "$ROOT/backend" && conda run -n dataq --no-capture-output alembic upgrade head >"$RUN/alembic.log" 2>&1)
  (cd "$ROOT" && conda run -n dataq --no-capture-output python -m backend.scripts.seed_dev >"$RUN/seed.log" 2>&1)
  (cd "$ROOT" && nohup conda run -n dataq --no-capture-output \
      uvicorn backend.app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$API_PORT" >"$RUN/api.log" 2>&1 </dev/null & echo $! >"$RUN/api.pid")
  for _ in $(seq 1 40); do
    curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}/api/v1/me" >/dev/null && break; sleep 1
  done
  curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}/api/v1/me" >/dev/null || { echo "api did not come up"; tail -20 "$RUN/api.log"; exit 1; }
  # The seed carries no llm_settings row; the LLM captures need a saved, enabled
  # OpenAI-compatible config so a fresh stack regenerates the same images. The
  # key is a placeholder (Ollama ignores it); Test only shows OK when a server
  # answers at DOCS_LLM_BASE_URL.
  curl -sf -o /dev/null -X PUT -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    "http://127.0.0.1:${API_PORT}/api/v1/admin/llm" \
    -d "{\"provider\":\"openai_compatible\",\"model\":\"${DOCS_LLM_MODEL:-qwen2.5:14b}\",\"base_url\":\"${DOCS_LLM_BASE_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1}\",\"api_key\":\"docs-capture-placeholder\",\"structured_output\":\"prompt_json\",\"enabled\":true}" \
    || { echo "could not seed the LLM provider config"; exit 1; }
  # Optional: a real Snowflake reader connection + suite, for the SQL-generation and
  # suggest-checks captures (both need to introspect a live table — a fake config
  # errors on every call). Skipped when DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT is unset, so the base
  # capture set still works with no warehouse credentials at hand; export it (plus
  # DOCS_SNOWFLAKE_USER/_SECRET, the rest default to the harness reader's shape —
